reviews.text: I have published a video review for the game which can be accessed at: https://youtu.be/Dc1PG6mpw-Y In short, this is a masterclass in arcade high score chasing tricks based game design. This is the cornerstone of what indie excellence represents. It aims to do just a couple of things, but it does them to a crisp perfection in all aspects, whether it be controls, style, soundcape. It's the total package. It brings all the smiles to the yard, as well as those bittersweet moments of rage when you fail a massive combo chain. Do not sleep on it.

[b]"And I'm free Free fallin' Yeah, I'm free Free fallin'"[/b] Tony Hawks Pro Skater meets science fiction and intrusive thoughts. Freefall '95 has fun in spades, a story that gives context and a reason to falling through the sky, leaderboards, skill trees, challenges/endless runs, and side quests. Complete games without micro-transactions are a rarity these days. I'd recommend this future cult-classic '95 times over for its charm, fun factor, and completeness on launch. Bravo S-Bend Games.

This game is EXCELLENT. Both a total evolution of classic score attack trick-based games like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater as well as a loving homage. It's filled with all kinds of content, challenges, player expression, beats, secrets, and made by people who clearly love video games. This game absolutely deserves your attention and time.
Flow-state, high-scores, combo fun. The best falling-from-the-sky simulator on the market, 10/10. Will lose hours to this game.

This game is super fun so far. It really cool to see a game doing something a bit different and creative rather than sticking to the same styles and formulas. Also a good analogy for life - do as many sick tricks as you can before you die, and don't mind the snakes.

Tony Hawk's Pro Airline Passenger, life insurance pays out triple if you land some sick tricks before you hit the ground this game rules, unequivocally. you might not think this much passion and love went into a game fundamentally about falling to your inevitable death. you might not think a game about an airline disaster could be this funny and cool. you might not think it's a hyper-engaging gameplay loop with a cool Stephen-King-esque element to it. you'd be wrong on all counts. the price to value ratio is off the charts, this high-effort indie outing is SOLID in every sense. play this game. do a flip. then parlay that flip into a x20 combo and live forever.

This game has way more depth than it lets on. Challenges, objectives, upgrades, leaderboards, and once you progress enough, a roguelite mode, which is like a whole other game! Well worth the asking price

I received my copy to help put the game through its paces on the Steam Deck. Between the demo and full release I've put 20+ hrs into this game, with the majority of those hours on the deck. So until Valve get their own tests done: ✅ All functionality is accessible when using the default controller configuration ✅ This game shows Steam Deck controller icons ✅ In-game interface text is legible on Steam Deck ✅ This game's default graphics configuration performs well on Steam Deck Even on the hectic endgame difficulty with heaps of stuff on screen, framerate sits between 80-90, with easily over three hours battery life. The game is pure fun, pushing for highscores while working through the levels and earning coins for upgrades is my jam, the mechanics are clean and allow for some crazy moves.

Freefall '95 does everything an indie game should. In a world where AAA games regurgitate themes and gameplay of every other top selling franchise, we can look to folks like S-Bend Games to give us something a little more personal. Freefall '95 has you skydiving out of a plane wreckage, busting sick move into sick move, collecting chips, getting bitten by snakes, and zig zagging through the debris laden air in search of special items. It's fun from the first play, but the level challenges and global leaderboard will have coming back time and time again. Bravo S-Bend Games! (ignore the game time on this review, I played the demo for yonks (In Australia that means a long time))
So here I am Doing everything I can Holding on to what I am Pretending I'm a superman! 10/10 game rules

I recently flew on a commercial airliner for business. I felt lucky I got to sit in the front row with a window seat so I could stretch my legs and not be bothered by other people scooching by with their ass in my face so they can go pee or worse. When we got airborne naturally I busted out my deck and this was the first and only game I ended up playing on that flight. Little did I know at the time but the older gentleman sitting next to me in the middle seat was the flight Marshall and he was keeping tabs on me. At first he was making friendly small talk trying to get me to reveal small details about myself. I was getting annoyed. I wanted to play this brilliant indie game but he was so insistent. I got a high score of 38k on the first level by lighting myself on fire and getting bit by 5 snakes and that's when things started to take a nose dive. "Listen slim, I just got a high score of 38k, I don't want to be rude, but can you maybe gab the woman's ear off next to you and not mine? Can't you see I'm busy playing Freefall '95?" I asked him dismissively before returning my gaze to this glorious game. He spit on the floor of the plane, unbuckled his seat belt, stood up, pulled out his revolver from his ankle holster, pointed it at my face and said: "What I see is a terrorist practicing terror on their terror practice device." Then he ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the hammer of his gun back and stared me straight in the eyes while I looked up at him like a deer in headlights and everybody around us who heard was cheering him on for being a hero and saving them. Even the stewardess looked at me like I was Satan and refused to take my drink order even though I had done nothing wrong. He handcuffed me, read me my rights, and instructed me that upon landing I would be escorted to the nearest black site to "await my trial" as a suspected terrorist. He also said he would be confiscating my terror device and instead of putting it away in a bag as evidence for the rest of the flight he was glued to it like a mosquito sinking down deeper into a jar of honey. He couldn't stop playing it. He even got up and took it with him to the bathroom. I was pleading with him to let me go and that this was all just a misunderstanding but he put his headphones on to ignore me and to listen to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' soundtrack. Right before we descended to land he makes a fist and exclaims to himself "YUSS!" as he taps me on the shoulder and shows me the screen. He got a high score of 39k and a dumb smug smile on his twisted mustached face to go with it. Now I'm writing this from my cell using a phone that was smuggled in by some ungodly means and still smells please send help.

This is not a hard no. Certain people will enjoy this. Given that Steam still has no in-between yes or no and this game at the time of writing has 0 negative reviews, I will throw in some observations that may put people off. + Nice tunes + Good price + Flash game vibes + Some character customization (unnecessary in this type of game, but appreciated) * Meta game progression in terms of HP, abilities, score multiplier, etc. - Lots of objectives like "land into a specific object" or "collect these specific items from the map", given that you are given no directions you end up moving around at random until you come upon these. A certain perk helps, but doesn't completely remove the issue - Grabbing debris to boost off of it feels unnecessarily risky, not only because anything nearby can hit you, but you are at the mercy of whether the debris starts spinning like mad or refusing to spin at all - Challenge mode has walls which can be used to cheese some of the challenges by drifting into a wall and almost bringing down momentum to a complete halt - Anytime the level objective has to do with "find X special items" in large amounts, I feel like the only time I succeed these is when I get lucky and find them in suitcases. I know some of them are stable items on the map but not only are they far away from each other, some of them are too time-consuming to grab - Roguelike mode essentially has the same levels as story/challenge modes but you have objectives like "find 6 wallets + 5 cell phones + do X tricks" etc, each objective giving you a passive/active ability as a reward. Success comes partly down to remembering maps so that you know exactly which direction has the most cell phones for instance, but the amount you need to collect is not the same each time. Combine this with suitcases dropping random items and frustration is unavoidable, given that one of the (optional) objectives of a roguelike mode is to not fail a single objective in any level - In the base game, things like snakes/alcohol/fire obscure visiblity, more so the more of these you collect in a short period of time, which is manageable in campaign levels, but absolutely terrible in the punishing roguelike mode (which is what they realised, having added a roguelike mode specific perk that has a chance to negate this visibility debuff) The demo available gives some idea of the gameplay which gives a good initial impression. It's just that I felt the experience got worse the further I played and the more these things started to grind my gears.

I usually try and find the prettiest, wisest, most smart boy set of words to describe a videogame - like it's more legitimate, like it makes this more real and important - but this is Fun, but It's fun in the same way that The Bible is 'The Holy Book'. It's the purest definition of goofy concept skill dependent well-scored videogaming delight, straight to you on any toaster computer you've got - in an era where most of us are gonna be stuck with the computer we have for The Forseeable Future and videogames are just going to get greedier, more complex, scarier and worse for The Foreseeable Future. When the world gets you down, you can make the freefall guy hit the ground and suddenly everything feels a bit more okay. Along the process he'll get bit by a dozen snakes and drink five bottles of bubbly and if you're real good you'll crash into The Yeti and die that way and I dunno, the analogy falls apart there; but the game is extremely excellent and you should have no doubts about playing it. Disclosure: I am a multiple world record holder and a true sicko, but I also doubt anybody that isn't 'a sicko' would wanna play the plane crash score attack awesome videogame.

Freefall '95 is very good at what it does. What it does is a Tony Hawk-esque sequence of short trick combo runs in a nicely animated two dimensions. The soundtrack is limited, but good for the vibe. The amount of content on offer for a game at this price is actually quite surprising in a good way. If I have a complaint, it's that the way the mechanics escalate difficulty is often finicky without opening up more depth to stringing combos together. This isn't always the case - e.g. kicking ducks is a fun thing which does add things you can do with the combos - but it is *mostly* the case. Adding things that attack you does definitely add difficulty. I just wish the move set could be expanded or refined to make sure there is always a parry. What is here is satisfying enough to keep me playing just to rank higher on the scoreboards. That's doesn't often happen.
Playing this, I realised we should normalise saying rad again over sick or cool. PS: I'm playing it on PC, and right away, I can see that the experience will be tenfold better on a handheld.
